audience.programmeDescription: Maastricht Business Engineering combines mathematics, engineering and business. Students apply those subjects in projects on market research, circular design, engineering and commercialisation before completing a thesis research project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: One UCR option combines sustainable technology and business. The other concentrates on software, modelling and data in a business context. Maastricht adds a longer sequence of engineering projects and laboratory work and a required internship and thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The standard pathway includes 45 EC of choices from the Business Engineering list and a 20 EC thesis package, including 2.5 EC of preparation.

componentNotes.y3-04: Students must be in year three and complete all first-year components before starting the thesis research. The Internship Office approves participation.

programmeLabels: Bachelor Business Engineering at Maastricht University
Sustainable technology, quantitative methods and business
Computational modelling, data and technology business

notes.text: UCR brings together sustainable materials, product prototyping, energy design, computing and business. Maastricht builds on a dedicated sequence in engineering fundamentals, materials, industrial processes and experimental laboratory work, with projects that apply those subjects.

Maastricht requires nine 5 EC choices from its Business Engineering list and a 20 EC thesis package. The package includes preparation, an internship, and an individual paper, presentation and defence. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the displayed 180 EC schedule.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.text: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the world. It supports the development of core personal and academic skills that enhance critical thinking and independent learning. It seeks to improve and develop academic writing and presenting skills and helps students develop the foundational skills and attitudes to reflect on societal issues and engage with societal partners.

ENSSUST313.name: Research in a Sustainable Delta
ENSSUST313.text: In this project course you will work in small teams of two or three students on a research problem relevant for sustainability in the broadest sense. We are looking for collaborations with local companies and other institutions. The research questions are supplied by a regional institution or company that is active in areas related to sustainability in the broadest sense. In this way it is guaranteed that the research projects are indeed relevant for the Zeeland delta. Furthermore, students will have access to expertise and/or facilities of the external partner, which will broaden their perspective. Usually, there will be one person affiliated with the external partner organization involved with a project team as external advisor

BENENTR111.name: Consumer Product Design
BENENTR111.text: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products. Design and development involves interviewing customers, brainstorming, laboratory experiments, quantitative modeling, constructing a prototype, and considering protection of intellectual property.
